claims.text: Assessment as-of date for the event study whose risk cells are compared here.
Forecast issue vintage used by the assessment.
Indonesia probability of government revenue loss in the first modeled year, conditional on the stated macroeconomic path.
Indonesia probability of government revenue loss in the second modeled year, conditional on the stated macroeconomic path.
Thailand probability of government revenue loss in the first modeled year, conditional on the stated macroeconomic path.
Thailand probability of government revenue loss in the second modeled year, conditional on the stated macroeconomic path.

Thailand shows a higher conditional probability of revenue loss than Indonesia in each of the two modeled years, so Thailand exceeds Indonesia on the per-year loss probabilities available for comparison.

The requested cumulative two-year (joint) loss probabilities for Indonesia and Thailand were not present in the fixed evidence packet, which was truncated under cell caps; only the annual per-country probabilities were available. Combining the two annual probabilities into a cumulative probability is an unsupported recomputation and was not performed.

limitations: The requested cumulative two-year p_revenue_loss cells for Indonesia and Thailand are absent from the fixed evidence packet (truncated before those country-year-range rows); only a single country cumulative cell for Australia was included.
Probabilities are reported in the tool's native probability unit; conversion to percentages was not performed because no conversion tool is available in this fixed-evidence single-response mode.
Per rules, the two annual probabilities cannot be averaged or multiplied to derive a joint two-year probability, so no cumulative figure is submitted for either country.

These are conditional scenario probabilities of a government revenue shortfall relative to a no-event counterfactual, not total-economy losses or sovereign default probabilities; the model does not claim causal identification.
Historical input provenance is incomplete and the assessment is marked recomputable: false; findings are for inspection only.
Validation diagnostics are conditional and final-vintage; convergence alone does not establish predictive skill.

response.reasoning_content:
User wants Indonesia vs Thailand cumulative (2026–2027) p_revenue_loss. But packet is truncated; country-level cumulative cells for IDN and THA "2026–2027" are not present (only AUS cumulative). Available: IDN 2026 0.5971, 2027 0.5325; THA 2026 0.6512, 2027 0.5869. Cumulative (joint two-year) probabilities for IDN/THA are not in the packet — cannot average or multiply. Report missing, but can report per-year percentages. Percentages: 59.71, 53.25, 65.12, 58.69 — but numeric claims must use exact tool value and unit. Should I convert probability to percentage? No convert tool; fixed evidence. Submit probability values with unit "probability" or "percent"? Values are probabilities; converting to percent requires multiplying — that's a supported trivial conversion? Rules say "For conversions first call convert_units" — no such tool available. Safer to submit probabilities with unit "probability" and note in text. But user asked "as percentages". Hmm. Multiplying by 100 is deterministic; but instructions insist numeric claims use exact tool value. I could submit value 59.71 unit "percent" — but not the tool's exact value. Risky. I'll submit probability values with unit "probability" and note in limitation that percentages would require unit conversion not available in fixed evidence... Actually simpler: include both? No—single exact value. I'll submit probabilities and mention in limitation that percent conversion wasn't performed. Alternatively submit numeric claim with value 59.71, unit "%", text citing the evidence—this misstates the tool value. Stick to probability unit.

Actually, maybe I can do the conversion myself and state it in a descriptive claim? Descriptive text must avoid digits. Just do probability claims and a limitation noting percent conversion unavailable.
